Tune Imputation for a Whole Data Set

Source: R/tune_impute_workflows.R
tune_impute_dataset.Rd

Extends [tune_impute_workflows()] — which benchmarks recipes and models for predicting **one** numeric variable — to a whole data set, so the user does not have to loop it per variable. With `engine = "workflows"` (default), each incomplete numeric column is tuned in turn with [tune_impute_workflows()] (same `recipes`, `models`, `folds`, `grid` and `race`, with the seed advanced by one per variable so each variable's folds are reproducible and distinct), and the tuned imputations are combined into one completed data set. With `engine = "missforest"` or `"missranger"`, the whole data set is instead imputed by sweeping `mtry` with [missforest_sweep_mtry()] / [missranger_sweep_mtry()], which already operate on full data but only tune `mtry`; extra arguments (`mtry_values`, `ntree` / `num.trees`, `parallel`, `max_pct_missing`, `checkpoint_dir`, `shard`, ...) are passed through to the sweep.

Usage

tune_impute_dataset(
  data,
  targets = NULL,
  engine = c("workflows", "missforest", "missranger"),
  exclude = NULL,
  recipes = NULL,
  models = NULL,
  folds = 5,
  grid = 10,
  race = TRUE,
  seed = 123,
  verbose = FALSE,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'impute_tune_dataset'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

data

A data frame.

targets

Character vector of columns to impute, or `NULL` (default) for every incomplete numeric column ( `"workflows"` engine) or every incomplete column (`"missforest"` / `"missranger"` engines). For the forest engines `targets` only selects which columns are summarised in `$summary`: the sweep imputes the whole data set, so non-target incomplete columns are filled in `$data` as well (see the Forest engines section).

engine

`"workflows"`, `"missforest"` or `"missranger"`.

exclude

Character vector of columns to hold out of the imputation entirely (identifiers, time columns). Passed through to the sweep for the forest engines; for the `"workflows"` engine the columns are simply never targets and are never used as predictors either (they are dropped from the tuning data).

recipes, models, folds, grid, race, seed, verbose

Passed to [tune_impute_workflows()] for the `"workflows"` engine.

...

For the forest engines, passed to [missforest_sweep_mtry()] / [missranger_sweep_mtry()] (for example `mtry_values`, `ntree`, `num.trees`, `parallel`, `max_pct_missing`, `checkpoint_dir`, `shard`).

x

The object to print (the result of the function).

Value

A list of class `impute_tune_dataset` with

per_variable

named list of per-variable [tune_impute_workflows()] results (`"workflows"` engine), or the single sweep result (`"missforest"` / `"missranger"` engines, under `sweep`)

summary

one row per imputed variable: `variable`, and for the `"workflows"` engine `best_workflow_id`, `rmse`, `null_rmse`, `rse` and `n_imputed`; for the forest engines `best_mtry` and `best_error`

data

`data` with every target column filled in; for the forest engines, every incomplete column except `exclude`d ones (see the Forest engines section)

engine, targets

the engine used and the variables imputed

How the per-variable fits combine

Each variable is tuned against the **original** data (the other columns as they stand, with the recipe's own median/mode imputation of predictors), not against already-imputed values, so the result does not depend on the order variables are tuned in. The completed data takes each tuned variable's column from its own fit. Imputations are **not chained**: an earlier target's tuned imputation is never used as a predictor for a later target, and no sequential (chained-equations) imputation is intended here. A variable that is complete, or that is not numeric, is never a target for the `"workflows"` engine; the forest engines impute every column they are given (numeric, factor and character) except `exclude`d ones.

Forest engines impute the whole data set

With `engine = "missforest"` or `"missranger"`, the sweep ([missforest_sweep_mtry()] / [missranger_sweep_mtry()]) is run on the whole data frame, not on `targets` alone, so `$data` has **every** incomplete column filled in — not only the columns named in `targets` — except columns in `exclude` (and columns held out by the sweep itself for exceeding `max_pct_missing`). `$summary` still reports one row per target only, so a non-target column that was filled is not listed there. When `targets` is `NULL` (the default) this is invisible, because every incomplete column is then a target; it only matters when `targets` names a subset. If only the target columns should be filled, use the `"workflows"` engine, or pass the non-target columns in `exclude`.

See also

[tune_impute_workflows()], [missforest_sweep_mtry()], [missranger_sweep_mtry()]

Examples

# \donttest{
ok <- vapply(c("workflowsets", "finetune", "tune", "rsample", "parsnip", "workflows", "yardstick"),
             requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)
if (all(ok)) {
  d <- mtcars
  d$mpg[c(3, 11, 20)] <- NA
  d$hp[c(5, 15)] <- NA
  res <- tune_impute_dataset(d, folds = 3, race = FALSE)
  res$summary
}
#> # A tibble: 2 × 6
#>   variable best_workflow_id  rmse null_rmse   rse n_imputed
#>   <chr>    <chr>            <dbl>     <dbl> <dbl>     <int>
#> 1 mpg      base_lm           3.81      5.79 0.433         3
#> 2 hp       base_lm          36.8      73.6  0.250         2
# }
